sports.headline: Morocco plans Swiss appeal after CAS reinstates Senegal as AFCON 2025 champions
sports.summary: The Court of Arbitration for Sport unanimously overturned CAF's decision to award the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations title to Morocco, which had given them a 3-0 forfeit win. Senegal's 1-0 win in the January final stands. CAS has since explained its reasoning. It found that the AFCON articles Morocco relied on did not apply, and that the referee's decision to resume the match was binding. CAF has accepted the ruling. Morocco says it will seek relief at the Swiss Federal Tribunal. The verdict itself came on 24 November, just before the 48-hour window. The dates for this item are inferred from relative timestamps, so treat the date as approximate.

fashion.headline: Isabel Marant names former Courrèges CMO Therese Lundström as chief marketing officer
fashion.summary: Lundström succeeds Sophie Condroyer and reports to CEO Catherine Jacquet, who took over in June. She will oversee global marketing, communications, press, celebrity relations, events and visual merchandising. Her CV includes Courrèges, Dries Van Noten and Givenchy. The appointment is part of a leadership reset at the French label.

marketing.headline: The Ordinary swaps Black Friday sales for a blood drive as other brands also opt out
marketing.summary: The Ordinary is closing its stores and website today, for the seventh year running. Its Fifth Avenue store in New York and its Toronto store become blood donation sites. London and Copenhagen offer blood-type testing. The campaign is backed by a $125,000 commitment from parent company Deciem and runs under the banner "Not Everything We Need is For Sale". Reuters also reports that Italian fashion brand Pinko is sitting out Black Friday for the first time.

marketing.headline: Coca-Cola drops AI for its 2026 holiday ad and goes live-action
marketing.summary: After two years of AI-generated holiday spots that drew backlash, Coca-Cola's new "Enjoy Joy" campaign uses real actors. The company says it is not ruling out AI for future ads. It also says the earlier AI ads passed its own Christmas benchmarks. Fast Company frames the switch as a vibe shift in public attitudes to AI advertising.
